narrative.overview:
Enote is a physical document made digital. The visual system starts from a single reference: the hand-written remission note that Xiera's baker hands the driver before loading the truck. That object is warm, worn, authoritative. It has no decoration beyond function: a number, a list of products, a destination, a stamp. The interface must feel like that document elevated, not like software that replaced it.

The surface itself is dusty rose — not a background tint but a material. Cards emerge from it in near-white warmth. Burgundy wine is the only accent, used exclusively for brand identity, primary actions, and note numbers (the most critical data on any screen). Cormorant Garamond heads the note number and modal titles; DM Sans carries everything workers need to read quickly. Shadows are warm-tinted (sepia base, never pure black) and stay low-profile except on modals.

This system explicitly rejects: the blank-canvas SaaS aesthetic of Notion and Linear; the grey-grid density of enterprise ERP like SAP; and the dopamine-reward palette of consumer delivery apps like Rappi. Enote must feel like it was designed by someone who knew the bakery, not by someone who knew Figma.
keyCharacteristics: Committed color strategy: dusty rose surface is the canvas, not a background tint.
Serif for identity, sans for operation. The pairing is strict and non-negotiable.
Status is unmissable: four semantic color states are the most visible system in the UI.
Shadows are warm-tinted and restrained. No pure-black rgba anywhere.
Touch targets sized for bakery conditions: busy hands, wet surfaces, quick glances.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Vino de la Tierra (#7A3045) is prohibited on decorative elements, secondary text, supplemental icons, and hover underlines. Its role is action and identity only. Its authority comes from rarity.

rules.name: The Warm Neutrals Rule
rules.body: No pure-black shadows, no cold grey borders, no #fff backgrounds. Every neutral references the brand hue even at near-zero chroma. rgba(44, 24, 16, α) is the shadow primitive for all elevation.

rules.name: The Cormorant Boundary Rule
rules.body: Cormorant Garamond is prohibited in: button labels, form field text, data table cells, error messages, badge text, and any context below 1rem. It lives exclusively in the brand mark and note numbers.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never use rgba(0, 0, 0, α) for shadows. The sepia-tinted shadow base unifies depth with the overall palette. A pure-black shadow on a terracotta surface is immediately wrong.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A card that doesn't respond to hover gets no shadow. The button shadow is a tactile affordance, not a decoration.

dos: Do use rgba(44, 24, 16, α) as the shadow base for all elevation without exception.
Do reserve Cormorant Garamond for the brand mark, modal titles, and note numbers only.
Do show all four status states with their full color triad (bg + text + border). Never communicate status with color alone.
Do keep all touch targets at minimum 44×44px.
Do use #F5EDEB (Crema de Pan) as the secondary surface for toolbars, form sections, and modal footers.
Do size the wine accent #7A3045 to convey authority: primary buttons, brand mark, note numbers.
donts: Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe accent. Use a full border, tinted background, or leading icon instead. The existing .indicator-new, .indicator-modified, and .diff-alert violate this rule and must be corrected.
Don't use Cormorant Garamond in button labels, form inputs, table cells, badge text, or any text below 1rem.
Don't use pure-black shadows or cold grey borders.
Don't make Enote look like a SaaS product (Notion, Linear, Jira): no blank white backgrounds, no cold blue accents.
Don't make it look like enterprise ERP (SAP, Excel-like): no dense grey tables, no deep hierarchical navigation.
Don't make it look like a consumer delivery app (Rappi, Uber Eats): no neon colors, no gamification.
Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere in the interface.
Don't use the wine accent #7A3045 for decorative purposes.
Don't show a spinner in the center of content during loading.
